Management says successful Q4 execution could put ONDS at a $1 BILLION annualized revenue run rate exiting 2026. This isn’t one contract or one opportunity. Revenue growth, organic backlog growth, new orders, and multiple programs entering delivery are all pointing in the same direction. That’s why I believe the guidance is achievable and why I’m increasingly bullish heading into November 12.

items.content_excerpt: $ONDS Definitely worth a read. items.content_excerpt: $NVDA !.As economists and investment managers at Bloomberg and MarketWatch have explained, the market is currently undergoing a paradigm shift. Investors have become far more selective, and the historical perception of technology companies has evolved. While they were once viewed as entities that generated mountains of cash without requiring heavy physical investment, they have now transformed into infrastructure behemoths—heavily laden with assets, debt, and expenses. The next phase of the artificial intelligence revolution is the "proof" phase—a stage where Wall Street is no longer satisfied with promises about the future, but instead prices in tangible risk for any company reporting negative cash flow.

items.content_excerpt: $AAPL :-As economists and investment managers at Bloomberg and MarketWatch have explained, the market is currently undergoing a paradigm shift. Investors have become far more selective, and the historical perception of technology companies has evolved. While they were once viewed as entities that generated mountains of cash without requiring heavy physical investment, they have now transformed into infrastructure behemoths—heavily laden with assets, debt, and expenses. The next phase of the artificial intelligence revolution is the "proof" phase—a stage where Wall Street is no longer satisfied with promises about the future, but instead prices in tangible risk for any company reporting negative cash flow.

items.content_excerpt: $META As economists and investment managers at Bloomberg and MarketWatch have explained, the market is currently undergoing a paradigm shift. Investors have become far more selective, and the historical perception of technology companies has evolved. While they were once viewed as entities that generated mountains of cash without requiring heavy physical investment, they have now transformed into infrastructure behemoths—heavily laden with assets, debt, and expenses. The next phase of the artificial intelligence revolution is the "proof" phase—a stage where Wall Street is no longer satisfied with promises about the future, but instead prices in tangible risk for any company reporting negative cash flow.!

items.content_excerpt: $PLTR I benefited greatly last earnings on this stock…this time even a 2-3% post-earnings pop could be a bull trap. At a $442B market cap, PLTR is priced for perfection. Q2 growth was exceptional, but the bar is now extremely high. A $2.18B revenue / $0.41 EPS consensus means simply beating estimates may not be enough. Without a major guidance upgrade, expect profit-taking and valuation compression. AI stocks are vulnerable as investors reassess sky-high valuations and future returns. Calls bought into earnings risk a double hit: reversal in share price + IV crush. Puts could benefit if the selloff is large enough to overcome premium decay. My aggressive target: $130-$140 by Nov 30, a 24-29% decline from Friday’s $184 close. Great company doesn’t mean great stock at any price.

items.title: @BiotechSwings For $TGTX , should not need any CVR becuase for all assets, projections and as part of that assumptions can be made and prici
items.content_excerpt: @BiotechSwings For $TGTX , should not need any CVR becuase for all assets, projections and as part of that assumptions can be made and pricing agreed upon. However, if not, then, maybe after a cash base amount is added for each of the following, then, perhaps separate CVRs for (1) Myasthenia Gravis, (2) Schizophrenia, and (3) Azer-Cel. Lots of lessons have learned in the biotech industry – the hard way – by both the business folks and attorneys. This would start with any CVR should be realistic; tradable; not subject to any time constraints; and have payment structures that allow for partial payouts based on achieving some milestones rather than an all-or-nothing scenario. And most important regarding the acquirer’s obligations -- rather than “Commercially Reasonable Efforts” a combination of the following is better: Best Efforts, Diligent Efforts, and/or Obligatory Actions.

items.title: $TGTX If there is a buyout, then a friendly buyout is best for everyone. If not because of MW or whatever, then, it’s interesting to note th
items.content_excerpt: $TGTX If there is a buyout, then a friendly buyout is best for everyone. If not because of MW or whatever, then, it’s interesting to note that Sanofi has significant experience with hostile takeovers: Genzyme Corp. 2010-2011, (an American pioneer in rare disease biotech) acquired to pivot into biologics, multiple sclerosis, and rare diseases to offset impending patent cliffs. Paid $20.1 B with a CVR that was supposed to give an additional $8.3B. The CVR covered multiple drugs and ultimately backfired due to delays and accusations of corporate bad faith. Aventis in 2004, a rival pharma giant much larger than SNY at the time, acquired to achieve survival-driven scale and create a national European champion. Paid $65B Moral of the story: No CVRs with ANY buyout purchaser.

items.content_excerpt: $XOM $CVX $OXY $XLE $USO CONFIRMED: OPEC+ HOLDS DECEMBER OIL PRODUCTION TARGETS STEADY OPEC+ officially announced Sunday that seven major producers will maintain existing production targets through December. KEY DEVELOPMENTS: • No additional production-target increases for December. • Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman participated. • Gulf oil production remains constrained by disruptions related to the Iran conflict. • Approximately 2 million barrels per day in broader OPEC+ production cuts remain in place through year-end. • Next meeting scheduled for November 29, with 2027 production policy becoming a major focus. MARKET TAKEAWAY: The decision removes uncertainty surrounding December production policy but does not resolve ongoing supply disruptions. Oil prices will remain sensitive to developments involving the Strait of Hormuz, actual export volumes and geopolitical negotiations. OFFICIALLY CONFIRMED — NOVEMBER 1, 2026. items.content_excerpt: Ukraine ended a two-week self-imposed pause on energy infrastructure strikes early Friday by hitting a major oil refinery in Russia’s Samara region Kyiv's decision to resume strikes follows an intensifying wave of Russian aerial bombardments targeting civilian centers and critical infrastructure. On Thursday alone, Russian missiles & drones killed at least 27 civilians & injured over 100 across Ukraine. Moscow is systematically targeting Ukraine’s power grid & heating systems ahead of winter to make major urban areas uninhabitable. President Trump has publicly blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for driving up global fuel prices. However, energy analysts overwhelmingly attribute broader market volatility to the military conflict between the U.S. and Iran, rather than defensive operations conducted by Kyiv. Kyiv’s battlefield capabilities were further restricted when $SPCX imposed speed limits on Ukraine’s military-grade Starlink terminals starting Oct. 14, reportedly at the request of CEO Elon Musk. The throttling paralyzed key Ukrainian military drone operations for 10 days before full service was restored on Oct 24. Ukrainian military leadership had exercised self-imposed restraint on refinery strikes to navigate delicate diplomatic relations w/ Washington. However, President Zelensky has established a firm boundary: Ukraine will only halt strikes on Russian oil infrastructure if the West provides guaranteed protection for Ukraine’s own energy grid. In the absence of those guarantees or effective US deterrence, Kyiv must act unilaterally to ensure its survival. The Trump Admin is unwilling to deter Russian aggression or protect Ukrainian civilian infrastructure $VLO $XOM $LNG $VG

items.title: US refiners hit highest utilization rates (95% from May to Sept) - highest since 1998 EIA: “High international demand for US distillate fuel
items.content_excerpt: US refiners hit highest utilization rates (95% from May to Sept) - highest since 1998 EIA: “High international demand for US distillate fuel oil exports has kept refinery outputs elevated" Since 1991, US refinery utilization has averaged 92% from May to September, compared with 88% across the other seven months. US refineries typically ramp up production during the summer months to meet soaring gasoline demands & then lower rates across the remaining months of the year As we moved into Oct, US refinery utilization rates did dip slightly from their impressive summer highs, though they continue to hover above the 5-year seasonal avg for the first 3 weeks of the month. A temporary slowdown could affect inventory levels Further, despite achieving the highest refinery utilization levels in more than 2 decades this summer, it’s essential to recognize that total US refinery output hasn’t peaked alongside the utilization rates. The overall output has only been the highest since 2019, driven by a -4% decrease in refining capacity since then. This means that while refineries are running at higher rates, their total production capacity has diminished Fed: As refined product inventories have declined, the difference between the price of oil and the wholesale prices of diesel, gasoline & jet fuel has increased well beyond normal. These differences, known as crack spreads, have exceeded levels last seen in 2022 following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine & the subsequent market disruption Taken together, refining capacity curtailment & depleted inventories are driving a blowout in fuel prices $VLO $XOM $SHEL $PSX $BP

items.title: Despite that WTI in triple digits, WCS (used by used refiners) is trading at a discount of $20-$25/barrel vs typical $12/barrel On Wednesday
items.content_excerpt: Despite that WTI in triple digits, WCS (used by used refiners) is trading at a discount of $20-$25/barrel vs typical $12/barrel On Wednesday, the differential was recorded by some reports even higher, at above $30/barrel WTI is sold at a higher price largely due to being easier to refine & good for making gasoline & diesel b/c low-density & low sulfur content, compared to the heavier, sour blend WCS US refiners—especially in the Midwest (PADD 2) & Gulf Coast (PADD 3)—have spent billions building multi-billion-dollar coking & hydrocracking units specifically engineered to process heavy, sour crudes. They cannot efficiently run light, sweet shale oil (like Permian WTI) through these heavy units without drastically reducing refinery throughput & margins Note: Moving heavy oil via ocean tanker from Venezuela to Texas is a short 3-to-5-day sea voyage. Even w/ recent elevated tanker rates, maritime shipping costs for that short Gulf run range b/n $1.50 to $3.50 per barrel & to move the same to Mid-continent US refineries, costs would exceed $8.00 to $15.00+ To move Canadian crude all the way down to Texas, WCS must travel thousands of miles via overland pipeline (like Enbridge or Keystone) & then downstream from Cushing, Oklahoma, to the Gulf Coast. Tariff tolls & pipe shipping costs for WCS down to the Gulf total $7.00 to $12.00+ per barrel & Mid-continent US refineries, tariff tolls & pipe shipping costs are b/n $4.00 & $6.00 per barrel Therefore, the WCS discount fully offsets the expensive overland pipeline freight to the Gulf & in fact grows Mid-land & Gulf refiners margins $VLO $PSX $XOM $BP $SHEL

items.title: Global refining crisis is worsening, as war damage to Middle Eastern refineries & Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian facilities severely
items.content_excerpt: Global refining crisis is worsening, as war damage to Middle Eastern refineries & Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian facilities severely restrict fuel supplies IIR: Over 12% of global refining capacity is off-line Ten years ago, European countries were closing refineries while Gulf oil states were building new ones. Now, many of these refineries have been damaged in the war b/n the US/Israel & Iran and Russia & Ukraine The Ukrainian army has launched more than 100 drone attacks on Russian refineries over the past few months. Some 30 refineries have been targeted, representing 80% of the country’s total refining capacity. Pre-war capacity was 6.1Mbpd vs now at 1.6Mbpd (19 refineries are offline completely & damaged several others). In all, Ukraine has taken out 59% of Russia’s fuel-making capacity. Before the strikes, the Russia was one of the world’s top suppliers of diesel, accounting for roughly 10% of the global market, but Moscow suspended exports in July to protect its domestic supplies. Trump Admin deal w/ Russia only brings in 75K barrels Rumour: US oil industry executives didn’t advocate for a diesel deal w/ Russia - they offered a different idea to the Trump admin last month: ask China to boost refinery output Note: President Trump has threatened to restart hostilities against Iran after the midterm elections on Nov 3 Rumour: Washington had warned its Gulf allies to prepare for “a short, intense military campaign after the US midterm elections,” This means that Iran will retaliate, & refineries in the region would be among the obvious targets The US-Iran War in the Middle East has led to more than a dozen direct attacks on refineries throughout the region, which together have an operating capacity of 7.6Mbpd The damage to these facilities has reduced fuel production capacity by more than 1Mbpd, including at Saudi Arabia's Jazan facility, which was hit by Houthi militants in Sept & remains completely offline. The situation is dire in Saudi Arabia, which has seen a roughly 25% drop in its oil refining capacity because of attacks & logistical bottlenecks Note: Yemeni Houthis just claimed responsibility for their latest attack on Saudi infrastructure: the Ras Tanura refinery, which has a capacity of 550Kbpd President Trump has repeatedly blamed Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries for high fuel prices, while playing down the impact of the conflict in the Middle East that halted oil-tanker traffic thru the vital Strait of Hormuz until recent weeks US is exploring other ways to try to ease fuel prices. Among them is invoking the Cold War-era Defense Production Act to spend up to $150M to expand refining capacity. Any investments, though, could take years to bear fruit given the complexities of refining facilities & the logistics of supplying them w/ crude. Typically, big upgrades for large refineries cost multiple billions of dollars & not millions $VLO $PSX $SHEL $XOM $SU
